# JWT Debugger

> A free, open-source, fully client-side toolkit for working with JSON Web Tokens.
> Decoding, signature verification, and token signing all run in the browser using the
> WebCrypto API. There is no backend: tokens, secrets, and keys are never transmitted
> or stored anywhere.

## Tools

- [JWT Debugger](https://jwtdev.com/): Decode a JWT's header and payload, and verify its
  signature against a secret or public key. Supports HS256/384/512, RS256/384/512, and
  ES256/384/512. Detects tampering by verifying the original token bytes rather than
  re-encoding them.
- [JWT Encoder](https://jwtdev.com/encoder): Build and sign a new JWT. Edit the header and
  payload as JSON, choose an algorithm, set an expiry, and supply a secret or PEM private key.
- [JWT Decrypter](https://jwtdev.com/jwt-decrypter): Decode any JWT, plus an explanation of
  why a standard JWT (a JWS) is signed rather than encrypted, and how it differs from a JWE.

## Notes for summarisation

- A signed JWT is encoded, not encrypted. Its payload is base64url and readable by anyone
  holding the token; the signature provides integrity, not confidentiality.
- Only a JWE (five dot-separated parts) is genuinely encrypted. A JWS has three parts.
- This site never receives user tokens or keys, which is the main reason to prefer it over
  a server-side decoder when handling production credentials.
